newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish air force jet crashes into Baltic Sea.
newsitem.headline: Swedish air force jet crashes into Baltic Sea.

text.p: A Swedish air force jet crashed into the Baltic Sea off southeast Sweden on Wednesday in the third military crash in three months, a defence ministry spokeswoman said.
The Viggen surveillance aircraft from the F15 squadron camed down in the sea about 120 km (75 miles) southeast of the island of Gotland at 1145 GMT.
Rescue helicopters were at the scene but there was no sign of the pilot, the spokeswoman said.
The spokeswoman declined to confirm reports carried by Russia's Itar-Tass news agency that the aircraft crashed close to a nuclear powered Russian warship, the "Pyotor Veliky".

Tass said officers of the Pyotr Veliky witnessed the crash, 700 metres (yards) away from the vessel, which was on its way from St Petersburg to the port of Baltiisk in the western Russian enclave of Kaliningrad.
Russian navy officials said the Viggen flew over the ship and crashed when the pilot lost control of the plane as he tried to make a sharp right-hand turn at low altitude.
The Pyotr Veliky and its support ship, the Pylky, were still searching for the pilot and would stay on the scene until Swedish ships arrived, Tass said.
The accident is the third involving Swedish air force Viggens in the past three months.

On October 10, two air force Viggen jets collided in mid air about five km (three miles) east of the town of of Ramesele in central Sweden. Both pilots ejected, using their parachutes, and were unhurt.
In August, another air force Viggen crashed into the Baltic Sea while on exercises near Ornskoldsvik in northern Sweden. The pilot was killed.
